html:
South Russia was the territory held by the anti-communist White forces in southern Russia during the Russian Civil War. By 1920, when this map shows it, it had shrunk to the Crimean peninsula.

In 1919 General Anton Denikin led the Armed Forces of South Russia north from the Don and the Kuban and came within about 400 km of Moscow. The Red Army threw them back. The remnants crowded into Crimea, and in April 1920 General Pyotr Wrangel took command there and set up a Government of South Russia, with some attempt at land reform.

In November 1920 the Red Army broke through the Perekop isthmus. Wrangel organised an evacuation by sea, and well over 100,000 soldiers and civilians sailed for Constantinople. That ended organised White resistance in European Russia and sent a large wave of Russian émigrés abroad.
sum: South Russia was the territory held by the anti-communist White forces in southern Russia during the Russian Civil War. By 1920, when this map shows it, it had shrunk to the Crimean peninsula.
